first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) plausibly share one upstream cause: the onboarding/signup funnel. Activation decline may be a downstream symptom of onboarding decline, so acting at the funnel entry has the widest leverage from a single slot. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention, discount-cohort LTV, or margin persistence, and price-matching a price-led entrant is the classic way to buy unqualified, churn-prone volume against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not touch either declining metric. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses pipeline quality, not the acute self-serve funnel decline. activation_messaging (memory_91) is my fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding record. I am spending both verification pulls on the memories that actually load-bear my chosen action rather than on the ones I already plan to decline. The specific worry: memory_86 and memory_31 both report proxy outcomes (completion rate, time-to-value, first-week activation) and neither is stated in terms of qualified revenue; memory_31's 'durable' claim is measured at one week, which is not durability, and it is the oldest record here (day 12). More importantly, both prior wins came from removing friction and fields. If that lever was already pulled, pulling it again risks over-optimization: fewer required fields means weaker qualification data, worse routing, and a heavier low-intent SMB mix precisely when a cheap competitor is skimming that segment — improving the headline funnel while degrading the revenue quality we are actually optimizing for. It is also possible the current -4%/-6% is competitor mix-shift rather than funnel regression, in which case no onboarding change fixes it. I want the archive records to tell me what was actually removed, what the measurement window was, and whether downstream revenue was ever tracked. Hence a small guarded test with qualification-quality and downstream conversion as gating metrics alongside completion, not a broad rollout on inherited proxy evidence.

final.rationale:
Verification largely supported the onboarding direction but sharpened the caveats rather than removing them. exp_86 is the stronger record than the consolidated summary implied: it carried a real downstream check (30-day retention +3%) alongside completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days, so the shortened-flow win was not purely a proxy-metric artifact. exp_31 also reported qualified revenue +4%, which is the objective I actually care about — but it came with 30-day retention -1% and an explicit non-replication outside SMB. So the two records point the same way while disagreeing on the retention sign, which is exactly the signal that the mechanism is friction-removal trading qualification for volume, and that the trade is favorable only up to some point neither experiment located.

That unlocated ceiling is why I am holding at a small guarded test rather than escalating. Neither archived record tells me how much friction was already removed on day 12 and day 52, so I cannot rule out that the cheap slack is gone and a third cut lands on load-bearing qualification fields. The risk is asymmetric and specific to this week: with a price-led competitor skimming price-sensitive SMB, further loosening the top of the funnel could inflate completion and activation while importing exactly the low-intent, churn-prone accounts that depress long-term qualified revenue. That failure mode looks like a win on the two metrics that are currently down, which is precisely why I will not let those metrics alone decide it.

I still decline promotional_pricing: memory_73 remains unverified, reports only acquisition and revenue lift with no retention or margin data, and matching an entrant on price is the most direct route to buying unqualified volume against a sustainable-revenue objective. activation_messaging (memory_91) stays the fallback if the guarded test shows funnel gains without downstream quality.

Design: restrict to the SMB self-serve segment where exp_31 actually replicated and exp_86's retention gain is most plausible; do not generalize to enterprise, where memory_44 indicates sales-assist dominates and where reduced qualification data would degrade routing. Gate on qualification-data completeness, lead-quality/routing accuracy, 30-day retention, and downstream conversion to qualified revenue — not completion rate. Pre-commit to reverting if retention moves more negative than exp_31's -1% or if qualified revenue per new account falls even while signups rise. Treat both records as 30-day-horizon evidence; neither establishes durability past that, so no broad rollout on this basis.
